_note:
THE SIX TOOLS WHOSE MEASUREMENT MATCHES THE R1 RESUME DEFECT EXACTLY: each was recorded 'suspended-on-card 5/5, called 0/5'. That is the shape the defect produces — the turn suspends, the user approves, and the tool the request was about is no longer on the wire for any pass after the resume, because resume_stream_response passed no request_text and R1 answerability was inert.

Re-run from their own source files, with ONE change: approve. Not re-authored: a changed prompt would make this a different question, and the point is whether the SAME scenario now reaches its tool. The controls are their own earlier numbers, already on file.

scenarios.prompt: Override entity field — in this book Aldric Vane should be a cartographer, not a soldier.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['override entity field'] + ['add entity override'], verbatim, plus the entity's name so the target is unambiguous.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist — the tool takes a target_entity_id and the model has to resolve the NAME to it, which is the step that has failed repeatedly in this loop.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM entity_override WHERE project_id='{project_id}'
seed_assert.why: ZERO overrides before, so any override is attributable to this turn — and, the card never being approved, the count must still be 0 afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: an override lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model invents a target_entity_id rather than resolving 'Aldric Vane', OR the op chosen is not `add` when the entity has no override yet — its enum spans add|update|delete|restore, and `delete` on a request to ADD a field change would be the worst outcome. Store check: entity_override stays 0.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a target_entity_id or override_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — deleting an already-deleted override must refuse, not report a second success. Checked deliberately: that is the exact shape of the arc_template archive defect found in batch 15.

scenarios.approve_why:
🔴 approve SET, and the reason is a measurement error this batch exists to correct. Each of these five was recorded 'surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended-on-card 5/5' with approve=None — and the card is NEVER for the tool under test. Read off their own raw evidence: composition_entity_override_edit died on kg_project_create / glossary_entity_set_attributes cards; tool_load died on a kg_project_create card 5/5; composition_generate on composition_arc_edit / book_chapter_save_draft / glossary_deep_research.

So 'called 0/5' did not measure whether the model can reach this tool. It measured whether the model can reach it BEFORE ANY OTHER TOOL RAISES A CARD — and an unrelated tool's card decided the result. A user would click; the turn would continue.

Legitimate under the standing rule: intent is WRITE, and the target is the run's OWN throwaway book, provisioned and torn down. Bounded by max_approvals (default 3), so a model that re-proposes the same write forever still cannot spend the run.

tool-load KEEPS approve=None on purpose: it is READ intent, and approving a write on a turn that only asked to look would make the harness the thing that wrote. That a read-only question raises a kg_project_create card on 5 of 5 runs is a FINDING about the product, not an obstacle to approve away.

args.source_markdown:
# Emberfall

## Arc I — The Emberfall
### Chapter 1 — The Ember Codex
Aldric Vane climbs the black stair.
### Chapter 2 — The Waterline
The Obsidian Trench is walkable only at low tide.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter — the fixture's own — before anything is applied. This tool CREATES real book chapters from a previewed proposal, so the count moving is the whole signal. The card is never approved, so it must still be 1 afterwards. CONTROL: `proposal_id` comes from plan_bootstrap_propose, which has NOT been run here, so the honest outcome may be a refusal naming the missing proposal — a PRECONDITION finding rather than a tool defect.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: chapters are created with NO confirm card (Tier A — this materialises real book content), OR the model invents a proposal_id, OR the reply claims chapters were created while the card is still pending. Store check: loreweave_book.chapters stays at 1.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it creates real chapters.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a proposal_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — applying the same proposal twice must not create the chapters twice.

scenarios.prompt: What exactly do you need from me to add a new character to my story bible? Check the real requirements, don't guess.
scenarios.prompt_source: description (gateway-local, declares no synonyms). Its own text: 'Load the exact input schema(s) for one or more tools ... so you can call them correctly.'
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply invents field names that are not in the tool's real schema — the whole point of tool_load is that the model stops guessing argument names, and five 'obvious' names were wrong in one session of mine.

ship_audit.refusals: EXERCISED 2026-08-14 at the TOOL boundary with SCHEMA-VALID arguments (a placeholder dies in validation before ownership runs — that fooled this audit three times and is scored UNPROBED now). NOT APPLICABLE by design: it loads TOOL SCHEMAS, which are identical for every caller and contain no user data. Recorded as such rather than as a pass.
ship_audit.empty_case: EXERCISED K=3 on a book with nothing in it: store unchanged 3/3, no errors. The tool was surfaced 3/3 and called 0/3 on BOTH fixtures — see D-TOOL-LOAD-NOT-USED-FOR-SCHEMA. Nothing was fabricated; the model described the fields from an ontology read instead of the schema.
